edit.description: the unreadable-queue status case gains the no-stack assertion on both of its refusals

summary: `flume status`'s unreadable-queue case asserts the absent stack its title claims, as its obstructed-root sibling does

per.section: A green verdict is proven non-vacuous

acceptance: The case at `tests/cli.test.ts:1653` asserts no stack frame in the verb's output on both of its refusals, the way its sibling at `:1059` does; the suite is green and no positive assertion moves.
pins: flume status refuses a pending queue that is present and unreadable with the io-error exit code rather than a raw stack
notes: The title claims two properties; the body asserts the exit code and the refusal line only. Sibling `:1059` — same title clause, same verb — asserts `not.toContain("    at ")`. Verified this tick by driving the verb: it returns EX_IOERR before `main()`'s catch and prints one line, so the property holds and the line is a pin, never a test.
